A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TextOCVP and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original TextOCVP experiments on CATER and CLIPort, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, robustness tests, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds original segmentation-mask, controllability, decoder-comparison, and temporal-evaluation results.

M1.justification: Appendix F.8 introduces an evaluated variant replacing the simple CNN renderer with a VQGAN-inspired decoder containing residual and attention blocks. v2 only discussed stronger decoders as future work. The main TextOCVP architecture, predictor, objectives, and training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use CATER-hard and CLIPort Put-Block-In-Bowl, including modified instructions, unseen colors, and increased object counts. The eight-object evaluation already appears in v2 Appendix F.4. New mask, success-rate, and temporal measurements assess the retained prediction tasks.

E2.justification: v3 adds Copy-Seed and OC-module-only as evaluated comparators in the new segmentation-mask comparison (Table 8). The existing OCVP, Non-OC, SEER, MAGE, and MAGEDINO benchmark comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The main benchmark settings remain unchanged, but v3 substantially extends evaluation design: mask IoU with background filtering, a 100-sequence controllability test with three instruction variants and distance-based success criteria, and metrics across 40 prediction steps. It also compares decoder capacities of approximately 25M versus 13M parameters.

E4.justification: Appendices F.4–F.5 and F.8–F.9 add quantitative object-dynamics checks, systematic controllability analysis, a renderer-capacity ablation, and temporal error analysis. New per-object visualizations supplement these tests. The earlier architectural ablations, artifact-cropping analysis, and color/object-count robustness tests are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 9 reports controllability success rates averaged over five runs, and Figure 8 adds mean curves with standard-deviation bands. v2 already reported uncertainty for inference timings. The source of variation underlying the new curve bands is not specified.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. New results include mask IoU of 0.573/0.569 at horizons 9/19, controllability success of 0.83 on original instructions versus 0.82 averaged across variants, and larger-decoder LPIPS of 0.043/0.065 versus 0.062/0.078 (Tables 8–9 and 11). Figure 8 adds temporal degradation curves. Decoder differences concern different model capacities.

T1.justification: The slot-attention, rendering, and training-loss mathematics remain equivalent. v3 combines and renumbers existing reconstruction-loss equations without changing their substance. Neither version contains a theorem or proof contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the same prediction, performance, controllability, and robustness claims. The conclusion narrows prospective applicability from robotic world-model applications to progress toward manipulation in simulated robotic environments.

C2.justification: v3 adds limitations concerning intricate or deformable objects and missing part-whole hierarchies (Appendix A.1). It also discusses long-horizon metrics' sensitivity to trajectory timing (F.9) and suggests overfitting as an explanation for T5 fine-tuning degradation. These extend the retained interpretations.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 newly specifies Non-OC's convolutional block, average pooling, 512-dimensional embedding, and matched training schedule; this documents the existing baseline. Appendix F.8 describes the new decoder's components and parameter counts. Main training details and the project/code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Daniel and Tamar's DDLP and Esser et al.'s VQGAN references, removes the SAVi++ reference, and expands the explanation of representation and text-conditioning differences from MAGE in Appendix C.1. The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites and expands the experimental narrative in Sections 4.2–4.3, introduces finer numbered subsections, and reorganizes interpretability and robustness discussions across the main text and appendix. Existing object-count and attention-head analyses are integrated into the main narrative, while much of the method prose is retained.

P2.justification: The paper changes from a two-column to a single-column journal layout. Earlier qualitative and attention figures are merged and rearranged, robustness tables are consolidated, and Table 1 incorporates PSNR scores already present in v2's appendix. New tables and figures display mask evaluation, controllability, decoder comparisons, and temporal curves.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens previously qualitative object-dynamics and controllability arguments with quantitative checks, tests the decoder-artifact explanation, and improves baseline documentation and limitations. These support an incremental quality improvement. The controllability assessment remains preliminary: its mask-distance thresholds are unspecified, and MAGEDINO is not evaluated with that measure.
